verified_checks.source: Bakker-Filipazzi-Mauri-Tsimerman, 'Baily-Borel compactifications of period images and the b-semiampleness conjecture' (v2, 18 Dec 2025, 61 pp.)
verified_checks.what_was_read: Full text via curl + pdftotext: Sec. 1 (all main theorems 1.1-1.9, proof outline), Sec. 2.2-2.9 (Defs 2.8, 2.9, Lemma 2.16, Def 2.17, Rem 2.19-2.20, Lemma 2.21, Def 2.23, Thm 2.24), Sec. 3.6 Lemma 3.16, Sec. 4 in full (Thm 4.1, Cor 4.2, Examples 4.6-4.7, Remark 4.8), Sec. 5.1-5.4 (Lemma 5.6, proofs of Thm 5.3), Sec. 6.4 (Def 6.18-6.21, Constr.-Def. 6.23, Rem 6.26-6.31, Thm 6.28 with proof), Constr. 6.32, Sec. 7 in full (Thms 7.1-7.3, 7.6-7.8, Cor 7.9 proof, 7.3.1 stratification estimate). Keyword sweep of the whole text for adjoint/K+/general type/hyperbolic/Iitaka/subadditivity/numerical dimension; reference list checked.
verified_checks.finding: (1) Main theorems and exact hypotheses. Thm 1.2/5.2 and Cor 1.3/4.2: for ANY polarizable integral pure VHS with unipotent local monodromy, the Griffiths bundle extends amply to Y^BB of the period image, hence is semiample (no extra conditions; integrability and torsion combinatorial monodromy (TCM) are automatic for Griffiths via Lemma 2.21 + GGR Thm 2.24). Thm 1.6/4.1: for a CY VHS (deepest Hodge piece of rank one -- exactly C1's setting) with unipotent monodromy, the Hodge bundle is semiample IF it is integrable (Def 2.17: wherever the Hodge line is not big, a subvariation containing it is isotrivial along curves through the generic point) AND has TCM (Def 2.23); Examples 4.6/4.7 show both are needed; Thm 1.7/5.3 builds Y^BBH under strict nefness + these conditions. Thm 1.5 (b-semiampleness): lc-trivial fibration from a pair with Delta EFFECTIVE over the generic point of X. Thm 7.3 (analytic): sub-pair allowed on the total space but 'the general fiber of f is an lc pair' (i.e. effective on the general fibre). (2) Sub-pairs. Def 6.18 (lc-trivial fibration) and Thm 6.28 (canonical bundle formula, moduli part = Schmid extension of the chi-isotypic Hodge line, cM ~ cN) DO allow sub-pairs: Constr.-Def. 6.23 writes Delta = E + F - G with G := ceil(Delta<0). This confirms ORB's stated use (Thm 6.28 for negative coefficients, not Thm 1.5). (3) Where effectivity enters. The conditions of Thm 4.1 are verified only under (‡): '(Y, Delta) is a klt quasiprojective pair over the generic point of X'. Thm 7.1 (integrability) uses [Amb05, Thm 3.3] or [PZ20, Thm A.12] to get isotriviality where M is not big; Thm 7.2 (TCM) uses Amb05 Thm 3.3/Prop 4.4 and finiteness of B-representations [HX16]. Ambro 2005 Thm 3.3 itself (read separately, math/0308143) requires 'B_eta is effective'. None of these applies to the kappa(F)=0 Iitaka sub-boundary, which is negative on the generic fibre. (4) Open status of the decisive condition. Remark 4.8 states the authors do not know whether a geometric CY VHS automatically has integrable Hodge bundle with TCM; it is known only for the middle-cohomology variation of K-trivial families (Thms 7.1-7.2). So applying Thm 4.1 to the least-index root-cover VHS of a kappa=0 fibre with negative generic sub-boundary is an open question that BFMT explicitly leave open, not a consequence. (5) No adjoint statement. BFMT contain no statement of the form K_S + jL big (or K + D, log general type, hyperbolicity) for the Hodge line or the Griffiths bundle on period images, do not cite Brunebarbe-Cadorel or any adjoint-bigness result, and do not mention Iitaka/C_{n,m}/subadditivity. Brunebarbe appears only in the acknowledgements; Deng 2023 is cited only for Borel extension. (6) Closest BFMT content to C1's rank-loss step: in the conditional Y^BBH picture (Thm 1.7 + Sec. 7.3.1, eq. 7.2) boundary strata are lower-dimensional images carrying quasi-finite CY period maps, so under integrability+TCM a boundary divisor mapping into the boundary of Y^BBH automatically has nu(L|D_i) < nu(L). C1's rank-loss lemma is thus an UNCONDITIONAL numerical shadow of a statement that BFMT obtain only CONDITIONALLY (and do not state numerically); it is not contained in BFMT. (7) Correction to the novelty pass: if the conditions held, M would be b-semiample (pulled back amply from the Hodge-BB image), which makes C1 unnecessary for C_{n,m}; C1's literal statement (K_S + jL big on the FULL period image S, where L need not be big) is not a one-line consequence of semiampleness of L, so 'trivial corollary' should read 'superseded/bypassed'. (8) AI disclosure: none in the full text or acknowledgements.
verbatim_quotes: Thm 1.5: "Let f : (Y, ∆) → X be an lc-trivial fibration from a pair (Y, ∆) such that ∆ is effective over the generic point of X. Then the moduli part M is b-semiample."
Thm 1.6: "If M_X is integrable with torsion combinatorial monodromy, then it is semiample."
Def 6.18: "Let (Y, ∆) be a sub-pair with coefficients in Q. A projective fibration f : Y → X is lc-trivial if (i) (Y, ∆) is an lc sub-pair over the generic point of X; ..."
Sec 7.1.1 (‡): "(Y, ∆) is a klt quasiprojective pair over the generic point of X"
Rem 4.8: "it is not clear to the authors whether a geometric polarizable integral pure CY variation automatically has Hodge bundle which is integrable and has torsion combinatorial monodromy."
Thm 7.3: "Assume that K_Y + ∆ ∼_{Q,f} 0 and that the general fiber of f is an lc pair."
verified_checks.effect_on_grade: Decisive precedent check PASSED at full-text level: BFMT neither contains C1 nor implies it; its semiampleness theorems require either generic effectivity (Thm 1.5, 7.3; conditions verified only under klt pair (‡) via Ambro Thm 3.3) or integrability + TCM, which BFMT explicitly say are not known for general geometric CY VHS (Rem 4.8). Risk (b) for BFMT Secs. 5-6 is closed (no K + jL statement). Residual: C1's rank-loss lemma is the unconditional numerical shadow of BFMT's conditional Y^BBH stratification (already listed as 'machinery'); this keeps C1 at N3 (provisional) rather than raising it. C1 confidence 0.40 -> 0.45.

precedent_checks.what_it_proves: (i) the period image has a functorial (Baily-Borel type) compactification on which the Griffiths bundle extends amply, so the Griffiths bundle is semiample; (ii) the Hodge bundle of a Calabi-Yau VHS is semiample under extra conditions -- a snippet gives them as 'M_X integrable with torsion combinatorial monodromy'; (iii) deduces the Prokhorov-Shokurov b-semiampleness conjecture, verifying (ii)'s conditions geometrically via Ambro and Kollar's minimal lc centres. search-snippet level only (arxiv.org, adsabs, researchgate unreachable from WebFetch: DNS failure); unverified
precedent_checks.does_it_imply_C1: No, as far as can be determined. The Prokhorov-Shokurov conjecture (PS09 Conj. 7.13, as restated in the Floris-Lazic travel guide arXiv:1907.10490) assumes the boundary is effective over the generic point; the Iitaka kappa(F)=0 reduction produces a sub-boundary that is negative on the generic fibre (ORD 01-introduction.tex 'The auxiliary sub-boundary in this formula can be negative on the generic fibre'; ORB introduction.tex:295-297 and reduced-root.tex:236-240: BFMT Thm 6.28 identifies the Hodge divisor with the moduli divisor 'permitting negative coefficients', but Thm 1.5 (semiampleness) needs generic effectiveness). If BFMT's CY-Hodge-bundle theorem applied to the least-index root-cover VHS (i.e. if its integrability/torsion-combinatorial-monodromy conditions could be verified there), M would be semiample, M = p*L with L ample, and C1 would be a trivial corollary (L big => K_S+jL big). Nobody, including BFMT, claims C_{n,m} as a consequence, which is indirect evidence that the conditions are not known in this case. Verdict: BFMT CONTAINS the machinery C1 is built from (Def 2.9 transcendental part, Lemmas 2.16, 5.6, Thm 6.28, the Baily-Borel picture in which boundary strata have lower dimension) but NOT the statement; it neither implies nor contains C1 on current evidence. Residual risk recorded in family_D.falls_to. [VERIFIED 2026-10-12 from full text: BFMT contain no adjoint/K_S + jL statement and do not cite Brunebarbe-Cadorel; generic effectivity is required for Thm 1.5 and Thm 7.3, and the integrability/TCM conditions of Thm 4.1 are proved only for klt pairs (‡) and are explicitly open for general geometric CY VHS (Rem 4.8). Correction: if those conditions held, C1 would be SUPERSEDED (M b-semiample) rather than literally a trivial corollary, since C1 concerns the full period image where L need not be big.]

candidates.statement: Y smooth projective, V a rationally polarized integral pure VHS on a dense open U whose entire highest Hodge step is a line, M in Pic(Y)_Q with tau*M ~_Q c J (extended highest line) on an alteration. Then after modification there is p:Y->S with connected fibres onto the (normalised) full period image and a nef L with M ~_Q p*L and K_S + jL big for j >> 0. Mechanism: Brunebarbe-Cadorel gives K_S + D big; rational minimality (BFMT transcendental part) + Andre normality + a tangential rank principle (or Ax-Schanuel in ORB) give nu(L|D_i) < nu(L) on every boundary component with N != 0 and every divisor fixed by finite inertia; section counting then removes D.

test2.evidence: Neither S, L nor 'K_S + jL big' occurs in the goal C_{n,m}. In L the closest statements are BC's 'K_S + D big' and Ambro's 'M = h*A, A nef big' (effective case), from which the C1 conclusion follows trivially only under the effective-boundary hypothesis that fails here. The NEED for some positivity of M on the kappa=0 locus is analytic (it is the classical obstruction Birkar names); the specific weakened target (adjoint bigness on the full period image, not semiampleness, not bigness of L) plus the rank-loss lemma that proves it are not subterms of L. Borderline because 'replace an open semiampleness statement by the weakest adjoint statement that Viehweg-type addition can use' is a natural goal-directed reformulation.
